newsitem.title: UK: British publisher Hodder has hardback sales boost.
newsitem.headline: British publisher Hodder has hardback sales boost.

text.p: British book publisher Hodder Headline Plc has seen a dramatic rise in hardback fiction sales since retail chains began to discount leading titles in 1995, chief executive Tim Hely Hutchison said on Tuesday.

"The biggest beneficiary of the Net Book Agreement (NBA) going is hardback fiction," Hely Hutchinson told Reuters, adding that sales of hardback novels by the company's top authors such as Stephen King had doubled or trebled.
The NBA, a century-old pact under which publishers would fix the British price of a title for an initial six months, collapsed two years ago when a number of leading publishers withdrew.
Its demise led to a wave of cost cutting in high street book chains while stores such as supermarkets began to sell popular titles at reduced prices.
Hodder Headline, which backed scrapping the agreement, said that the move had expanded the retail market for books.
The company earlier reported a 16 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 6.6 million pounds ($10.6 million). It left its dividend unchanged at 6.5 pence per share.
Hodder Headline shares were marked 1.5p higher at 217.5p on figures broadly in line with expectations.
Hely Hutchinson was cautiously optimistic about the current year after a promising start.
"1997 has started well and it is possible to detect signs of more robust UK consumer and educational markets," he said.
He said that the British retail market for books appeared to be improving after chains closed stores and reduced stock levels.
Britain represents Hodder Headline's main market but it is also active in English-speaking countries such as New Zealand, Australia and South Africa.
